answer: What survives to the pearl is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, converted to a slow vesting stream, no identity may audit its own recruit. The jetty holds work receipts rather than names, so the whisper of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread.
